notes:
Summary: Mid-market analytics SaaS building in-product assistant + semantic search. Started with Hosted API eval (fast onboarding) -> POC showed 2x perf vs earlier provider on generation latency for short-chat flows. Now negotiating Dedicated reserved pool for predictable throughput and data isolation. Key ask: pricing that supports 1) predictable monthly cost for steady-state usage, 2) burst headroom for product launches, 3) reasonable overage band during ramp.

POC highlights: 1) Hosted API quickstart (sandbox) — NPS from PM team favorable. 2) Evaluated embeddings for search; top-k reranking improved MRR on internal test queries. 3) Chat latency target: p95 < 200ms for short-turn chat flows, throughput target ~150 req/s aggregated.

Dedicated pricing conversation notes: - Want 3 commit tiers proposed: small (2x A40 equiv), medium (4x), large (8x). Prefer monthly ramp schedule: 50% commit first 30 days, 100% by day 90. - Burst: require burst-to-4x baseline for first 6 weeks of new feature launches; negotiate burst pool as billed at 1.5x base units. - Overage: customer wants capped overage multiplier; Redwood proposed 1.8x for on-demand tokens and compute, Pegasus pushing for 1.2-1.4x for first 3 months of ramp. - Ramp credits: request 2 weeks of free burst during GA. - SLA & audit: need SOC2 attestation, KMS integration for key-wrapping, audit logs forwarded to their SIEM. - Data residency: EU region requirement for EU customers (subset of accounts).

Stakeholders: CTO (Arjun Patel) - technical sign-off; Head of Product (Lena Morales) - usage patterns and launch windows; Procurement (Tom Bradley) - pricing and legal; Security (Mayumi Kato) - SOC2/KMS/pen test items.

Verbatim from call (09/10 pricing workshop): "We need predictability — finance will not sign open overage risk. If we commit, we expect burst and a ramp-friendly overage structure."

Next steps (short): finalize 1) commit sizes + ramp schedule, 2) concrete burst pricing and burst-time caps, 3) draft SOW with explicit overage formula and early-termination adjustments. Legal loop to start once financial terms agreed.
